title: Oil and Water
objective: After this level you can explain why oil and fresh water shape life in the Middle East.
summary: The Persian Gulf countries hold about half the world's proved oil reserves, but the region has very little fresh water, so Gulf countries burn oil and gas to desalinate the sea.

cards.headline: Kuwait has no rivers or lakes. So it drinks the sea.
cards.body: The country sits in one of the driest regions on Earth, on top of one of its richest resources. The trick of this level is how the second solves the first.

cards.headline: Half the world's oil, around one gulf
cards.body: The seven countries around the Persian Gulf hold about half of the world's proved crude oil reserves. That oil began as tiny plants and animals in ancient seas. Buried under sand, silt and rock, they were cooked by heat and pressure into crude oil. The land on top is bone dry. The rock underneath is loaded.

cards.fact: The region has about 6% of the world's people and less than 2% of its fresh water.
cards.context: That's the Middle East and North Africa. Remember Level 1: about 71% of Earth's surface is water. The catch: about 96.5% of Earth's water is in the oceans, too salty to drink. The region is surrounded by water it can't use as it comes.

cards.headline: Trading oil for water
cards.body: So the Gulf makes its own. Desalination removes the salt from seawater, and Kuwait gets about 90% of its drinking water that way. It takes a lot of energy, and the Gulf countries power it with oil and natural gas. The fuel under the sand turns the sea into something you can drink.
cards.callout: Oil and gas in, fresh water out

cards.headline: Oil and water: balanced
learned: Gulf countries hold about half of the world's proved oil
Oil formed from ancient sea life, buried and heated
The region has 6% of people but under 2% of fresh water
Desalination, run on oil and gas, supplies Kuwait

questions.prompt: About what share of the world's proved crude oil reserves do the Persian Gulf countries hold?

options.label: Nearly all
options.rationale: Other regions hold the other half.

questions.explanation: The seven Persian Gulf countries hold about half of the world's proved crude oil reserves.

questions.prompt: How do Gulf countries power their energy-hungry desalination plants?

options.label: With river dams
options.rationale: Kuwait has no rivers to dam.

options.label: With geothermal heat from the rift
options.rationale: The fuel is under the sand, not in the rift.

questions.explanation: Desalination takes a lot of energy, and the Gulf countries run it on their own oil and natural gas.

questions.prompt: Level 1 says about 71% of Earth's surface is water. Why is the Middle East still short of it?

options.label: Its seas are too far inland
options.rationale: The Gulf is right on the coast.

options.label: Almost all of Earth's water is salty ocean
Most ocean water is frozen at the poles
options.rationale: Most of it is liquid ocean, just salty.

options.label: The region lies far from any ocean

questions.explanation: About 96.5% of Earth's water is in the salty oceans. The region has plenty of sea but less than 2% of the world's renewable fresh water.
